question: What is the primary purpose of data management in midwifery research?

options.A: Speeding up the discharge of pregnant women
options.B: Increasing the number of hospital admissions
options.C: Reducing the cost of hospital drugs
options.D: Ensuring findings are trustworthy and reliable

explanation: Proper data management ensures that information collected from patients is accurate so that research findings can be trusted for clinical guidelines. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h1)

question: When does the process of data management officially begin in a research project?

options.A: At the very beginning with a clear protocol
options.B: When the research paper is ready for publication
options.C: During the final data analysis stage
options.D: Only after all questionnaires have been lost

explanation: Planning how data will be collected, stored, and managed must happen before any fieldwork or data collection begins. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h1)

question: When should data quality control measures primarily take place?

options.A: After the research paper has been published
options.B: During the fieldwork and data collection phase
options.C: Before the research topic is even chosen
options.D: Years after the study has ended

explanation: Catching errors while still in the field allows researchers to verify information with respondents before the project wraps up. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h2)

question: A research assistant records a newborn's head circumference as 120 centimeters. What does a quality control check show about this entry?

options.A: It is an impossible value that needs immediate verification
options.B: It proves the baby was born with a rare medical condition
options.C: It shows the measuring tape was brand new
options.D: It is a normal finding for a full-term Nigerian baby

explanation: An adult head is roughly 55 centimeters, so 120 centimeters for a newborn is biologically impossible and indicates a recording error. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of coding in research data processing?

options.C: Hiding the true identity of vulnerable patients
options.D: Translating descriptive responses into numerical values

explanation: Computers and statistical software analyze numbers much faster and easier than text, so words are converted to codes. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why must a coding frame be created before data collection starts?

options.A: To increase the total number of survey participants
options.B: To maintain consistency across different research assistants
options.C: To make sure patients pay their hospital bills on time
options.D: To prevent the computers from crashing during analysis

explanation: Having a set coding guide ensures that everyone on the research team labels identical responses with the exact same numbers. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is double-entry verification in research data management?

options.A: Interviewing every pregnant woman twice on the same day
options.B: Writing survey questions in two different Nigerian languages
options.C: Two different clerks typing the same dataset independently
options.D: Storing backup files on two separate flash drives

explanation: Double-entry helps catch typing typos by comparing two independent entries of the same source documents. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h4)

question: A data entry clerk types '450' instead of '45' for a pregnant woman's weight. Which tool helps stop this mistake during typing?

options.A: An extra copy of the research proposal
options.C: A range check built into the data entry mask

explanation: Range checks reject numbers that fall outside realistic biological limits, catching extreme typing errors immediately. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical goal of data cleaning?

options.A: Spotting and correcting anomalies in the dataset
options.B: Finding missing values in completed questionnaires
options.C: Checking frequency tables for unexpected wild codes
options.D: Recruiting more human participants for the study

explanation: Data cleaning happens after data collection is completely finished, so it does not involve recruiting new participants. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h5)

question: What does finding a code of '5' in a marital status variable with only options 1 to 3 indicate?

options.A: A computer virus corrupting the spreadsheet
options.B: An accurate reflection of Nigerian marriage customs
options.C: A wild code that requires checking the original questionnaire
options.D: A brand new statistical finding of great importance

explanation: A code outside the expected range is a wild code or error that must be traced back to the original paper form to fix. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h5)

question: What does data integrity guarantee in healthcare research?

options.A: That the hospital receives more funding from donors
options.B: That the research study finishes ahead of schedule
options.C: That patients never have to answer personal questions
options.D: That records remain accurate, complete, and uncompromised

explanation: Data integrity ensures that the information collected has not been tampered with, lost, or incorrectly altered. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why must completed questionnaires containing a patient's HIV status be locked away?

options.A: To ensure the paper forms do not get misplaced by the wind
options.B: To make it harder for research supervisors to do their jobs
options.C: To prevent the statistical software from reading confidential notes
options.D: To protect patient confidentiality and uphold research ethics

explanation: Healthcare data is highly sensitive, and researchers have a legal and ethical duty to protect participant privacy at all times. [learn more](BMP314_U2_T2#BMP314_U2_T2_h6)
